title: Clinical characteristics, treatment, and prognostic factors in patients with trilateral retinoblastoma: A retrospective cohort study
summary:
Trilateral retinoblastoma is a rare and serious childhood cancer. It occurs when a child with retinoblastoma, a malignant tumor of the retina, also develops a tumor inside the skull, most commonly in the region of the pineal gland or above the pituitary gland.
The aim of this retrospective study is to investigate the clinical course, treatment, and survival of patients with trilateral retinoblastoma. For this purpose, existing medical records will be analyzed. Particular attention will be paid to identifying clinical and imaging-related characteristics associated with survival.
The findings may contribute to a better understanding of the disease, help identify potential risk factors, and support improvements in the future diagnosis and treatment of affected children.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients diagnosed with trilateral retinoblastoma between 1970 and 2025.
